value.overview: The Ladder-backed Woodpecker (Dryobates scalaris) is a woodpecker recorded in the United States. Field recognition often comes from ladder-like black-and-white barring on the back, spotted underparts, buff or whitish face, and red crown on adult males. In the U.S. source data, it appeared in 8 state or DC summaries, including AZ, CA, CO, NM, NV, OK, TX, UT. It is most associated with Aridlands:  Desert Scrub and Forests:  Tropical Dry, and local season should be checked before trip planning.
value.classification: The Ladder-backed Woodpecker belongs to the family Woodpeckers in the order Piciformes. This is the practical birding classification used for the BirdIntel profile cache.
value.identification: Look for ladder-like black-and-white barring on the back, spotted underparts, buff or whitish face, and red crown on adult males. Also use size, posture, flight style, voice, behavior, habitat, and season. Plumage can vary by sex, age, molt, and light, so the safest identification comes from combining several field marks rather than relying on one color or feature.

value.dietFeeding: It eats insects and other arthropods taken from bark, branches, trunks, and sometimes the ground. It may also take fruit, seeds, or sap depending on season. Foraging usually involves climbing, probing, tapping, or flaking bark.
value.behavior: It climbs trunks and branches using stiff tail feathers for support. Calls, drumming, and repeated visits to favored trees are often useful clues. Many woodpeckers defend territories during the breeding season.
